title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page closes the '2e partie' of the notes, which compare the Cartier operator on de Rham cohomology with Frobenius eigenvalues. The setting is a proper smooth curve X (or its Jacobian A) over S = Spec F_p, or a finite field k.

The previous page sets up three things:
- the Hodge exact sequence 0 → ω = H^0(X,Ω^1) → H^1_DR(X/S) → R^1f_*O_X → 0;
- the fact that the Cartier operator C (transpose of Frobenius) kills the quotient R^1f_*O;
- the consequence that, over F_p, the nonzero eigenvalues of C on H^1_DR coincide with those on ω. By Katz (Manin's congruence), these are the reductions mod p of the eigenvalues of ℓ-adic (or crystalline) Frobenius that are p-adic units.

This page draws the consequences.
1. Forms with C̃ω = ω are, locally, logarithmic differentials df/f. These are the classes attached to relative divisors D with pD = div(f).
2. Such forms let one construct eigenvectors of Frobenius (ℓ-adic or crystalline) whose eigenvalues are ≡ 1 mod p.
3. A nonzero ω with C̃ω = ω exists iff some Frobenius eigenvalue is ≡ 1 mod p.
4. Grothendieck claims the F_p-dimension of {ω : C̃ω = ω} equals the number of Frobenius eigenvalues ≡ 1 mod p.
5. He also claims it equals dim_{F_p} of the p-torsion of rational points, pA(k), with A the Jacobian.

Modern form of point 5: dlog gives an isomorphism H^1_fl(X, μ_p) ≅ H^0(X,Ω^1)^{C=1}. Over a perfect field k, H^1_fl(X, μ_p) = Pic(X)[p]. Over a finite field Pic^0(X) = J(k) and Pic/Pic^0 is torsion-free, so the fixed space of C ≅ J(k)[p]. This is the classical Cartier–Serre description of p-torsion through logarithmic differentials. The count via eigenvalues comes from the Manin/Katz congruence: the characteristic polynomial of the Hasse–Witt/Cartier matrix agrees mod p with the unit-root part of the Weil polynomial. The page is a summary of known facts used to motivate the relative Picard variants that begin on the next page ('Variantes concernant des foncteurs de Picard relatifs').
errors: Point 4 is only an inequality in general. dim{ω : Cω = ω} = dim J(k)[p] = dim ker(F−1) on the étale part of J[p] is a geometric multiplicity. 'Number of Frobenius eigenvalues ≡ 1 mod p' (counted with multiplicity) is an algebraic multiplicity. They agree only when Frobenius/Cartier acts semisimply on the generalized eigenvalue-1 part; a Jordan block gives a strict inequality, e.g. J(F_p)[p] ≅ Z/p while eigenvalue 1 occurs twice.
'Congrue à 1 mod p' must be read modulo a prime above p in the field of the Frobenius eigenvalues (or as reduction in a residue field); this is left implicit.
The identification with pA(k) tacitly needs k perfect (finite) and Pic^0(X) = J(k). Both hold over finite fields, but this is not stated.

ideas.what: Forms fixed by the Cartier operator are exactly the logarithmic differentials df/f; they correspond to p-torsion in the Picard group / Jacobian
ideas.modern_name: Cartier isomorphism; dlog: H^1_fl(X,μ_p) ≅ (Ω^1)^{C=1}; Cartier–Serre description of J[p]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957–58), Serre (1958, Mexico symposium), later Milne (flat duality)

ideas.what: The nonzero eigenvalues of Cartier/Hasse–Witt are the reductions mod p of the p-adic unit Frobenius eigenvalues
ideas.modern_name: Manin's congruence (Hasse–Witt matrix vs zeta function mod p); unit-root part of Frobenius
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin (1961), Katz (cited on the previous page)

ideas.what: Number of Frobenius eigenvalues ≡ 1 mod p controls the dimension of the C-fixed forms, hence the p-rank of J(F_q)[p]
ideas.modern_name: p-torsion of J(F_q) via the Cartier operator / unit-root F-crystal

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a terse summary of classical facts: Cartier-fixed forms are logarithmic differentials, they correspond to J(k)[p], and the Manin–Katz congruence links them to unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues. It even overstates one equality (geometric vs algebraic multiplicity). Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: '(logarithmiques[?], en caractéristique[?])' should read '(ℓ-adiques, ou cristallins)'. This matches 'Frobenius ℓ-adique ou cristallin' on the previous page.
The operator in 'il existe ω avec F̃ω = ω' and in 'telles que F̃ω = ω' is the Cartier operator C̃ ('C̃ω = ω̃'), not F̃. This continues 'les ω tels que C̃ω = ω̃' from the previous page.
Line 2: a crossed-out word is replaced by an interlinear word, and the reading 'valeurs' is uncertain. Mathematically, 'vecteurs propres' (eigenvectors) is what is constructed.
Line 1 begins with an uncertain word, perhaps 'rel.' or 'ω'. The sentence continues the previous page: '...les ω tels que C̃ω = ω̃ sont loc. des différentielles logarithmiques'.
The parenthetical underlined with a triple line reads like '(certes ici !)' or '(cristallin ici !)'; it is uncertain, not 'formes (cristallines !)'.
Last line: the crossed-out word before 'pA(k)' is likely 'fondamentaux'/'fondamental' and is deleted. The surviving text is 'des groupes pA(k), A la jacobienne'.
